text: unverified: the new `Receipts (2026-09-16):` paragraph in `fleet/CONTRACT.md` pins literals that live in sibling-owned files this patch does not touch — `factsBlock` in `fleet/facts-block.mjs` and its `''`-when-none / newest-kept behaviour (task 4), the `20`-row cap, and the `driver:facts` `{label, task?, receipts: [ids]}` / `driver:finding` / `driver:finding-refuted` field sets emitted from `fleet/run-engine.mjs` and `fleet/publish-fold.mjs` (tasks 1–5, 7). All five Proof `Run:` greps exit 0, so this task's own legs (M1–M4) are settled

what is not settled from this diff alone is whether the contract's literals match what the sibling code actually emits. What would settle it: the post-fold suite on the integration branch — `fleet/tests/test_facts_block.mjs` (FACTS_ROW_MAX/FACTS_FIELD_MAX and the empty-render case) together with the engine and publish-fold receipt tests — read against this paragraph's wording after all seven tasks land. Grading minor because no edit to `fleet/CONTRACT.md` can verify it and the contract is the declared authority for these literals.

Global Constraint (prose, no `Check:` behind it): "The `FACTS:` block is bounded: at most 20 rows, each row's `read` and `against` at most 500 characters, so a block is under 24 KB". The diff enforces the two bounds it names — `FACTS_MAX_ROWS = 20` with `.slice(-FACTS_MAX_ROWS)` (fleet/facts-block.mjs:149) and `cut()` at `FACTS_FIELD_MAX` (fleet/facts-block.mjs:106-109) — but the third unbounded term in a rendered line, `row.paths.join(', ')` (fleet/facts-block.mjs:121), is not cut. Arithmetic: 20 rows x 1000 chars of fields = ~20 KB, header ~170, per-line furniture ~50 x 20 = ~1 KB, leaving roughly 2.8 KB of slack for 20 joined path lists — about 140 characters each. A `driver:finding` receipt whose `paths` is a task's whole FILES set (this run's task 2 carries five paths, ~185 chars joined) already sits at the boundary, and a wider task would cross it, so the constraint's stated "under 24 KB" consequence does not follow from what the module enforces. I take the constraint to require that the rendered block, not merely the row count and the two evidence fields, stay under 24 KB. The fix is not the implementer's: M2 spells the row line as `[<paths joined by ', '>]` with no cut, so bounding the joined list would diverge from the task's own Machine clause and from the byte-for-byte literal the exam pins at fleet/tests/test_facts_block.mjs:259-261 and 376-378 (and that Task 5 must match). The task text is where a `paths` cut — or an explicit acknowledgement that the 24 KB figure assumes small path sets — has to be stated.

`fleet/run-engine.mjs` (the `driver:wave-blocked` site): a `CONFLICT` epoch that narrated nothing mints a receipt whose `paths` is `[]`, which contradicts the plan's shared RECEIPT SHAPE literal ("`paths` is ... never empty") that this same task's `foldReceiptOf` honours by answering `null` on an empty `open`. `foldWave`'s `blocked(reason)` helper returns `{status: 'CONFLICT'}` from four sites that run before any `conflicts.json` exists — `fleet/run-engine.mjs:3836` (fold printed no verdict), `:3840` (fold parked N conflicts, written before the index in some kernel paths), `:3843` (fold exited non-zero with no `open`) and `:3846` (no conflicts count) — so `narratedPaths()` returns an empty Set and the row lands carrying `paths: []` together with an `evidence` object. That row is "a row carrying both keys", i.e. a receipt by the shared definition, but Task 4's matcher (M1: `paths` a non-empty array of strings) will never match it, so the reading is recorded in a shape nothing can render. The graded legs do not reach this path — leg (a)'s rig always narrates `a.txt` — so the exam stays green either way
guarding on a non-empty path list makes the wave-blocked site say the same thing `foldReceiptOf` already says.

unverified: M3 fixes `publishFoldEvent(row, open)` to take `run`, `attempt`, `base` and `resolverRetries` "from `row` as at BASE", and the diff transcribes that faithfully (`run: r.run`, `attempt: r.attempt`, `base: r.base`, `resolverRetries: typeof r.resolverRetries === 'number' ? ... : 0`). But the attempt row never holds those four at BASE: `record` at `fleet/publish-fold.mjs:473-496` writes only `tip`, `candidate`, `pushedHead`, `disposition`, `reason`, `path`, `pathsJoined`, `resolversDispatched`, `suite`, `checks`, `checkRetries`, and both append sites read `run, attempt, base` from the enclosing scope (`:501`) and `resolverRetries` from `record`'s own destructured local (`:477`). Leg (e) passes a hand-built row carrying all four, so the exam cannot see this. If Task 7 wires the sites literally as its Context prescribes — `eventLog.onEvent(publishFoldEvent(row, conflictsIndex()))` — the fresh row's `run`, `attempt` and `base` become `undefined` and drop out of `events.jsonl` on serialisation, and `resolverRetries` silently reads 0. Nothing inside this task's FILES can settle it: the signature is fixed by this task's Produces contract, so the fix belongs to Task 7's call site, which must hand in a composed row (`{ ...row, run, attempt, base, resolverRetries }`). What would settle it is Task 7's diff showing both call sites supplying those four values, and its rig asserting the appended `driver:publish-fold` row still carries `run`, `attempt`, `base` and a non-zero `resolverRetries`.

unverified: the global constraint "Every new event kind and every new event field is named in `fleet/CONTRACT.md`" is not satisfiable inside this diff. This task introduces two new event fields — `paths` and `evidence` on `driver:wave-blocked` (`fleet/run-engine.mjs`) and on `driver:publish-fold` (via `publishFoldEvent` in `fleet/publish-fold.mjs`) — while `fleet/CONTRACT.md` is Task 6's sole file (SIBLING FILES: 6). This diff correctly leaves that path untouched, and no `Check:` command backs this constraint in CHECK EVIDENCE, so it blocks nothing here. What would settle it is Task 6's diff naming `paths` and `evidence` under both the `driver:wave-blocked` and `driver:publish-fold` sentences, with the same bounded `{read, against}` shape these two sites mint.

unverified: GLOBAL CONSTRAINT "Every new event kind and every new event field is named in `fleet/CONTRACT.md`" is not satisfied by this tree. The diff adds two new event fields — `paths` and `evidence` on `driver:exam-run` (fleet/run-engine.mjs, the `runExam` appendEvent) and on `resolver:reply` (the emit inside `resolveConflicts`) — and `fleet/CONTRACT.md` at BASE names neither (no match for `evidence.read`, `evidence.against` or a `paths` field). The fix lies in `fleet/CONTRACT.md`, which is task 6's (popmechanic-ultrapowers#1csr) declared file and outside this task's FILES, so this diff cannot carry it and the constraint carries no `Check:` the driver ran. What would settle it: task 6's diff naming `paths` and `evidence` (with the `{read, against}` pair and the 500-character bound) in the CONTRACT's event vocabulary for `driver:exam-run` and `resolver:reply`. Graded minor so it does not stop a merge it cannot judge.

The resolver's own free-text `notes` rides verbatim into the receipt: `read: cutTo(res.status + ' on ' + conflict.path + (res.notes ? (': ' + res.notes) : ''))` (fleet/run-engine.mjs, the `resolver:reply` emit). M2 only requires `read` to begin with the status, so the notes are an addition, and they are worker-authored prose that a later task of this plan renders into a judge's `FACTS:` block. GLOBAL CONSTRAINT "A receipt states what was observed and never what to do … no rendered `FACTS:` line carries an instruction to a judge beyond the block's own header sentence" is a prose constraint with no `Check:` the driver ran, and this is my reading of it: the 500-character cut bounds the size of what a resolver can put in front of a judge but not its content, so a resolver whose `notes` read as instructions would have them rendered as a reading. The status, the path and the hunks file are all driver-observed and already satisfy M2

dropping the `res.notes` clause (or reducing it to a fixed marker that a note was left) would close the surface without touching any leg — legs (c) and (d) pin only that `read` begins with `BLOCKED` and that a `RESOLVED` row carries neither key.

`examReceiptOf` can return a receipt whose `paths` is empty, which the task's Context RECEIPT SHAPE forbids: "`paths` is an array of repo-relative path strings, sorted, de-duplicated, never empty". `sortedUnion(landings, files)` returns `[]` when both arguments are empty or all-empty-string, and nothing rejects that before the `{ paths, evidence }` literal is built (fleet/run-engine.mjs, the new export). It is unreachable from the engine's own call site — `examRunnable` requires `proofTests.length`, so `examLandings` is non-empty there — and no Proof leg pins it, which is why this is advisory

but the function is a shared pure export the Context says later tasks of this plan read the shape off, so a caller passing empty `landings`/`files` would get a row the shared literal says cannot exist. Either guard it (return `null`, or throw, when the union is empty) or say in the comment above the export that a non-empty union is the caller's precondition.

The AMENDMENTS entry declares that `scenario` "gained three optional knobs: `seed(runDir)` (called after the rig provisions the run directory and before the engine starts), and `implReply`/`fixReply`". The diff carries `implReply` and `fixReply` as declared, but there is no `seed` parameter anywhere in it

the seeding role is filled by `stateExams` — a specialised knob that writes `<runDir>/state-exams/task-<id>/<dir>/<file>` after `rig()` provisions and before `run()`, which is exactly the position and purpose the entry's `what` and `why` describe. Two further knobs the entry does not mention are also added to the same shared helper: `examSilent2` (leg (g)'s round-2 examiner that returns DONE and writes nothing) and `extra` (merged into `extraArgs`, used by leg (d)'s `reviewOnStateExams: true`).  Graded minor rather than blocking: the substance of the declaration is borne out — a knob in the declared position doing the declared job — and the `why` holds against the task text verbatim (leg (d) does need a state-exam record where `stateExamRowsOf` reads it back). The inaccuracy is the knob's name and an undercount, in an entry that declared an edit rule 9 never required to be declared: the file is inside this task's own FILES, no clause is read otherwise, and no existing leg is re-aimed — every added parameter defaults to precisely the rig's prior behaviour (`implReply`/`fixReply` fall through to `doneImpl(cwd)`, `stateExams || {}` writes nothing, `examSilent2` is `false`, `extra` merges empty), which the file's other legs passing green confirms. Fix is to make the entry name the knobs the lines actually carry.

unverified: the sixth Global Constraint — "Every new event kind and every new event field is named in `fleet/CONTRACT.md`, which wins over `fleet/RUNBOOK.md` on any literal" — is not settled by this diff. This task mints two event kinds absent at BASE (`driver:finding` at the review-round and hollow-exam sites, `driver:finding-refuted` at the three refutation sites) and adds two fields to an existing kind (`paths` and `evidence` on `handshake:finding`, via `raiseFinding`), and `fleet/CONTRACT.md` is untouched. That is correct conduct, not a defect of the diff: `fleet/CONTRACT.md` is a SIBLING FILES path, owned by task 6 ("The contract names the receipts, the block, the reading and the deletion rule"), so editing it here would itself be blocking under rule 3. The constraint carries no `Check:` command the driver ran, so this is grounded only in reading the prose. What would settle it: task 6's landed diff naming `driver:finding` `{task, round, severity, actor, detail, paths, evidence}`, `driver:finding-refuted` `{task, round, paths, evidence, verdict, refutedBy, detail}`, and the `paths`/`evidence` addition to `handshake:finding`. Flagged for the integrator to confirm at the fold, not for a fix round here.

unverified: the diff adds three module-scope helpers to `fleet/run-engine.mjs` — `reading` (the 500-character cut, 499 plus `…`), `evidenceOf`, and `pathsOf` (sort + de-duplicate + drop blanks) — none exported. Two siblings add near-identical logic to the same file: task 1 produces `examReceiptOf(...)`, whose contract spells the same 500-character bound, and task 2 produces `receiptPaths(list)`, whose contract is the same sort-and-dedupe over a string list. After the wave folds, `fleet/run-engine.mjs` will hold both `pathsOf` and `receiptPaths` doing substantially one job, and the 500-char cut spelled in at least two places. This task could not have avoided it — its Interfaces are `Produces: none` / `Consumes: none`, so it had no sanctioned way to reach the siblings' exports, and the duplication is the plan's decomposition rather than this implementer's choice. Not a reason to hold this submission
worth one pass at the fold to collapse `pathsOf` onto `receiptPaths` and `reading` onto whatever task 1's bound helper ends up named.

concern: plan-defect: M3's closing sentence (`evidence.against` is the finding's own `detail`) disagrees with legs (f) and (g) for cases (ii) and (iii). Leg (f) fixes `evidence.against` as the exam's red line beginning `the Proof's exam failed:` while the event's `detail` is the CONCERN
leg (g) fixes both as the rejection's own detail. Implemented to the legs, since the legs are what the exam asserts. Disclosure only — both legs pass as written.

concern: The receipt literal is implemented as three module-level helpers beside `tail` in `fleet/run-engine.mjs` — `reading`, `evidenceOf`, `pathsOf` — because INTERFACES gave this task no shared symbol to consume. Tasks 1 and 5 also write `fleet/run-engine.mjs` and may introduce their own copies
a fold that lands two declarations of any of those three names is a duplicate-const at module scope, not a semantic conflict.

concern: `fleet/tests/test_run_engine_state_handshake.mjs` is red at BASE and still red after this task, which does not touch it: its entire body is `import './exams/run_155/test_run_engine_state_handshake.mjs'` and that path does not exist in this tree. The Context sentence pointing at it as the at-BASE exercise of `raiseFinding` therefore names a file that is not here
M4 is covered by leg (i) of this task's own sim instead, on a fake-hub rig built in place.
